priority.override_reason: The user requested an iMac study of repeated cache probing and receiver-miss proof reuse. The fresh queue ranks hash-map seventh externally; three exact profiles show a 12-14 percent cold-read envelope and diagnostic counts confirm 3.78M repeated probes. Higher-ranked gaps remain controls. This is distinct from rejected T041 OwnSlot hot-answer expansion and T033 receiver-proof shortcuts.

mechanism.summary: Compact named reads perform their initial hot probe once. Preserve ordinary/exotic guards and full cache probing in the cold continuation; the direct captured-field-initializer entry performs its own first hot probe before that continuation. Keep cache coverage, replacement policy, value/layout guards and generic fallbacks unchanged.
mechanism.generality: Only control flow proving an earlier side-effect-free hot probe returned None admits the continuation. No workload name, property name, source text, bytecode template, iteration count or expected value selects it.
semantic_risks: Direct callers such as captured class-field initializers must retain their first hot probe.
Preserve ordinary/exotic classification, identity, layout, slot, descriptor and prototype guards. Getters and Proxies keep normal fallback.
Cache borrows must end before user code; retain weak ownership and invalidation after assignments, deletion, insertion, accessors and prototype replacement.

LTO and layout can move unrelated functions. Every case remains a control; no compiler/order-file tuning or favorable reruns are part of this attempt. Layout matching remains a limitation for production promotion.
